content:
# 屹立不倒

我从未像现在这样迫切地想写下这封月报。写作对于我来说，是重新梳理脉络的方式——把一个月的嘈杂整理出清晰的轮廓。而这个月，需要梳理的事实在太多。那就用最诚实的方式来写：先说我听到了什么，再说我怎么看。

## 我听到的

整整一个月，我都在和自己信任的对冲基金经理通电话。如果一定要用一个词概括大家的状态，那就是：惊魂未定。恐慌与困惑，几乎各占一半。和我聊过的人，没有谁听起来像是在掌控自己的投资组合；更像是他们的仓位正在反过来支配他们。

比起情绪，仓位更能说明问题。上海的交易台重仓存储芯片股——部分原因，是我几周前提过的总收益互换限制。为了缓解保证金压力，他们在全面抛售境内半导体个股，转买 DRAM ETF，以一篮子资产的敞口替代单一个股风险。香港则从中间一分为二，多空势均力敌。美国的长线资金还在观望——这里最重要的是，他们顾虑的并不是价格，而是仍不相信长期供货协议足以让存储行业摆脱周期股估值、获得成长股估值。至于宏观基金？他们卖掉了一切。存储、半导体，一个仓位都没留。

真正值得记录的，是这一切背后的争论，因为多空双方的逻辑都相当扎实。

多头的论点是这样的：供应链调研显示，价格与利润率维持高位的时间，会比任何人的模型预测得更久。市场对 2027 和 2028 年资本开支的预期还在不断上调。OpenAI 与 Anthropic 的收入增速毫无放缓迹象——Codex 的周活跃用户增长快到几乎无法在图表中呈现；而 Kimi K3 的技术报告读起来，简直像在逐项说明每一种半导体元件为何都成了瓶颈。宏观环境也算温和，CPI 与 PPI 双双降温。即便现货价格无法再涨，这些公司也终于有足够健康的资产负债表，通过回购和分红为股价提供支撑。更关键的是，OpenAI 与 Anthropic 正在大规模组建解决方案工程师团队，向金融、医疗、法律等垂直领域开发产品，在编程之外寻找下一条增长曲线。因此多头认为，即使存储行情降温，整个半导体板块的逻辑仍不会动摇。

空头的论证同样漂亮。高价不可持续，因为它最终会摧毁需求：客户迟早会抵制，政府也可能强行推动大规模扩产。价格将在第四季度见顶。2027 年的资本开支确有依据，2028 年的预算却仍充满变数。即使基本面足够稳健，这笔交易也已经拥挤到危险的程度；韩国散户手中的高杠杆，本身就是一场等待发生的事故。2027 年云厂商的资本开支计划固然激进，但其中相当一部分交付会被推迟——因为电力供应根本不足以让这些芯片投入运行。市场也找不到另一个像 AI 编程这样高速普及的应用，来填补中间的需求缺口。空头最有力的一点是：在*上行周期*中，涨价和更多长期协议都无法证明存储行业已经摆脱周期性。真正的考验只会出现在下行周期——当景气反转，存储厂商能否守住利润率底线。在此之前，存储既是整座 AI 大厦的核心，也是它最危险的软肋：存储行情一旦瓦解，其他一切都会跟着倒下。归根结底，存储和白银、原油、碳酸锂一样，仍是一种大宗商品。而每一种大宗商品在见顶时，看起来都像是划时代的投资机会——故事闪闪发光，基本面无可挑剔——直到下一刻，一切不再如此。

## 我的判断

先说美联储，因为第三季度的基调已经基本确定。我认为七月和九月加息的概率都很低。这轮通胀的导火索，是战争以及随之上涨的油价，而加息无法凭空增加一桶原油。服务价格也没有明显加速。提高利率解决不了真正过热的部分——面对这场火，它根本不是正确的工具。

比起议息会议，收益率曲线正在发生的变化更值得关注。即使政策利率被牢牢钉住，短端收益率仍在缓慢下行，长端却持续走高，反映市场正在计入更长期的通胀。长端利率居高不下，相当于悄无声息地向所有风险资产征收估值税。把 FOMC 之后的盘面与微软、Meta 的财报表现放在一起看，逐渐清晰的并不是信用*质量*问题，而是信用市场的*承载能力*问题。太多公司为了资本开支借入了太多资金。问题不在于这些债券有多危险，而在于债券市场根本没有足够的资金消化如此庞大的发行量。这是一场披着偿付危机外衣的流动性挤压。

再把战争叠加进来。如今的不确定性比三月战事刚起时更高，并非因为新闻标题更加刺眼，而是这场冲突演变为长期战争的可能性已经显著上升。与此同时，市场正带伤前行：刚刚发生的动量交易踩踏，是近年来最剧烈的一次。按照以往经验，它所需要的修复时间，甚至会超过 2024 年套利交易平仓后的恢复期。这样的骨折，不可能一周痊愈。

因此，我们的策略十分明确。微软大涨，Meta 重挫，两者的分化传递出一个清晰信号：在承压的市场中，资金奖励的是现金流——那些无需承担更多信用风险、也不必继续举债，仍能保持增长的公司。我们顺着这条逻辑，买入了一批现金创造能力强的大盘股，同时建立大规模对冲仓位，防范市场整体下跌。这个月不适合逞英雄。我们会等待市场企稳，等待波动率回归常态，然后再重新审视高贝塔标的，寻找那些确定性已经恢复的机会。耐心，再一次，才是我们真正的仓位。

## 最后再说一件事

我想向 Leopold Aschenbrenner 和 Situational Awareness 致意。我们自己的一组投资组合，也曾在同一轮抛售中险些遭到强制平仓，所以这番话更多出于感同身受，而不是幸灾乐祸：有一只基金截至六月的收益超过 400%，却在短短一个残酷的七月后，被迫清算全部公开市场仓位。保证金追缴到来后，它的多头与空头被打包成一笔交易，整体卖给了 Citadel。费城半导体指数较六月高点一度下跌近 29%，动量策略组合跌幅超过 50%。七月初还接近 450 亿美元的资产规模，几天之内就只剩约 100 亿美元。杠杆就是有这样的力量：两个星期四之间，它便能让全球表现最出色的基金，变成一则风险警示。

借用高中生的说法：兄弟替我们结结实实挨了一拳。整个板块反倒欠了他一份古怪的人情——有时，只有经历一次彻底的出清，市场才终于能够喘过气来。

我们还站着。向八月前进。

—— Atros W.M.

title: Still Standing
excerpt: I've never wanted to write one of these so badly. Writing is how I rewind the tape — how I sort the month from noise into something with a shape — and this month there was a great deal to sort.
content:
# Still Standing

I've never wanted to write one of these so badly. Writing is how I rewind the tape — how I sort the month from noise into something with a shape — and this month there was a great deal to sort. So let me do it the honest way: first what I've heard, then what I think.

## What I've Heard

I spent the month on the phone with hedge fund PMs I trust, and if I had to distill the collective mood into a single word, it would be *rattled*. Panicked and confused, in roughly equal measure. Nobody I spoke to sounded like they were in control of their book; they sounded like they were being controlled by it.

The positioning tells the story better than the sentiment does. The Shanghai desks are extremely long the memory names — partly a function of the total-return-swap restriction I flagged a few weeks back — and they're dumping mainland semiconductors across the board to buy DRAM ETFs, trading single-name risk for basket exposure to take the edge off the margin pressure. Hong Kong is split straight down the middle, bulls and bears in an even standoff. The U.S. long-onlys are sitting on their hands, and — this is the important part — it isn't about the price. It's that they still don't believe long-term agreements can drag memory from a cyclical valuation to a growth one. And the macro funds? They sold everything. Every memory and semi position, gone.

The debate underneath all of this is the one worth transcribing, because both sides are genuinely good.

The bulls make the case like this. Supply-chain checks point to prices and margins staying higher for longer than anyone modeled. Capex in 2027 and 2028 keeps getting revised up, not down. The revenue ramps at OpenAI and Anthropic show no sign of flattening — Codex's weekly active users are growing at a rate that's frankly hard to draw on a chart — and Kimi K3's technical report reads, if you squint, like a list in which every single semiconductor component is a bottleneck. The macro backdrop is benign, with CPI and PPI both cooler. And even if spot prices can't climb another dollar, these companies can defend their own shares with buybacks and dividends, because the balance sheets finally allow it. The kicker: OpenAI and Anthropic are standing up large teams of solution engineers to build vertical products — finance, healthcare, legal — hunting the next S-curve beyond coding. And even if memory itself cools, the argument goes, the broader semi complex stays intact.

The bears are just as fluent. Higher prices aren't sustainable; they're demand-destructive, and at some point customers push back or a government steps in and forces a brute-force capacity expansion. Prices peak in Q4. The 2027 capex is real, but the 2028 budgets are cloudy at best. Even granting solid fundamentals, the trade is dangerously crowded, and the leverage sitting in the hands of Korean retail investors is its own kind of accident waiting to happen. The 2027 cloud capex plans are aggressive, sure — but a meaningful slice of those deliveries slips, because the power isn't there to plug the chips into. There's no intermediate adoption story with the velocity of AI coding to bridge the gap. And here's the cleanest point on the board: higher prices and more LTAs during an *upcycle* prove nothing about cyclicality. The only proof that matters comes in the downturn — memory names holding the lower bound of their margins when the cycle rolls. Until then, memory is the core of the whole AI edifice, which cuts both ways: if the memory trade dies, everything dies with it. Because in the end, memory is a commodity like any other — silver, oil, lithium carbonate — and every commodity looks like a generational story right at the top, narrative and fundamentals gleaming, the moment before it doesn't.

## What I Think

Start with the Fed, because the Q3 tone is now mostly set. I put low odds on a hike in either July or September. The reason is that this inflation's fuse is the war and the oil price it's dragged higher, and a rate hike does exactly nothing to add barrels of crude to the market. Service prices haven't meaningfully accelerated. Raising rates simply doesn't address the thing that's actually running hot — it's the wrong tool for this particular fire.

What's happening in the curve is more interesting than what's happening at the meeting. The short end is drifting lower even with the funds rate pinned, while the long end is climbing, pricing in longer-term inflation. A long end that stays elevated is a quiet tax on the valuation of every risk asset in the building. And when I read the tape after the FOMC and the Microsoft and Meta prints together, the story that keeps resolving into focus isn't a credit-*quality* problem — it's a credit-*capacity* one. Too many companies are borrowing too much to fund capex, and the issue isn't that the bonds are risky; it's that the bond market doesn't have the money to absorb all of it. That's a liquidity squeeze wearing a solvency costume.

Layer the war on top. The uncertainty now is worse than it was in March, when the fighting first started — not because the headlines are louder, but because the probability of this hardening into a long war is materially higher than it was then. And the market is walking wounded: it just went through a momentum unwind unlike anything in recent memory, and by the ordinary math of these things, that takes longer to repair than even the 2024 carry-trade unwind did. You don't heal a break like that in a week.

So here's how we're anchored. Microsoft ripped and Meta got hit, and the message in that split is unambiguous: in a pressured tape, the market rewards cash flow — companies that can keep growing without reaching for additional credit risk or credit exposure. We leaned into exactly that, buying a set of big caps with strong cash generation and, at the same time, putting on large-sized hedges to protect against the broad-market downside. This is not the month to be a hero. We wait for the market to steady, for volatility to revert toward its mean, and only then do we rescan the higher-beta names for the trades where the certainty has come back. Patience, again, is the position.

## One Last Thing

I want to tip my hat to Leopold Aschenbrenner and Situational Awareness. One of our own books came uncomfortably close to being liquidated in the same wave, so I say this with more fellow-feeling than schadenfreude: a fund that was up more than 400% through June was, one brutal month later, a forced seller of its entire public book — longs and shorts sold in a single block to Citadel after the margin calls came. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell nearly 29% from its June peak, and the momentum basket dropped more than 50%. Assets that stood near $45 billion at the start of July were around $10 billion within days. Leverage does that. It turns the best-performing fund in the world into a cautionary tale between two Thursdays.

To borrow the way a high-school kid would put it: bro took a hard one for us. The whole complex owes him a strange, backhanded debt — sometimes the clearing event is the thing that finally clears the air.

We're still standing. Onward to August.

— Atros W.M.

title: 那不勒斯奶昔
excerpt: 就像它名字所取自的那款甜点，六月带着满满一桶各色滋味如约而至——三种截然不同的口味叠在同一个容器里，彼此之间界限分明，并不融合。那就一勺一勺来品。
content:
# 那不勒斯奶昔

就像它名字所取自的那款甜点，六月带着满满一桶各色滋味如约而至——三种截然不同的口味叠在同一个容器里，彼此之间界限分明，并不融合。那就一勺一勺来品。

![](/blog/june-2026-illustration.png)

## 第一勺：美联储

六月的 FOMC 会议，几乎是咄咄逼人的平静——不加息、不降息、没有新闻，更重要的是，没有担当。所谓"没有担当"，是指沃什主席明确表示，前瞻指引在他任内已经画上句号，未来美联储的沟通将刻意保持克制。这不禁让人想起格林斯潘？格林斯潘是谁？没错——正是这个意思。那是上个世纪的事了。

我不加掩饰地说：我完全不赞同这一改革。那套"让市场自行寻找效率"的老派央行哲学，根本无法映射到我们实际所处的时代。今日市场的复杂程度，比"以晦涩为智慧"的格林斯潘年代高出整整一个量级——更具反身性、杠杆更高、对每一个音节的反应都更加敏锐。切断沟通纽带、美其名曰"纪律"，是假设市场已经做好了迎接新丛林的准备。对此，我毫无把握。

## 第二勺：数据

CPI 和 PCE 双双略低于预期——幅度谈不上戏剧性，但足以给室内降一些温度。加息大合唱，可以预见地，又开始热身了。我高度怀疑这会成真。如果加息真的在桌面上，我不认为它会在中期选举前落地。有些歌，只有在选票数完之后才会开口唱。

## 第三勺：仓位

这才是六月真正交出成绩单的地方。

$NOK 给了我们等待已久的那波拉升，我们兑现了利润——然后立刻重新买回。我们认为这个标的在 7 月 23 日财报发布后具备重估潜力。数学并不复杂：即便在第一张 AI-RAN 订单入账之前，$NOK 的 P/E 也应当至少达到 $CIEN 的一半。目前它还没到，而这个缺口，就是这笔交易的逻辑所在。

$ORCL 则截然相反，经历了一个糟糕的月份——事实上是自互联网泡沫破裂以来最惨烈的一个月，走势极其难看。为什么？因为所有人都憎恨稀释，而甲骨文给了市场一份 200 亿美元的股权发行来消化。但让我们来捋一捋，而不是条件反射地回避。他们为什么不断稀释？这才是真正的关键。你不会为了踟蹰不前而募集这种规模的资金；你募集，是因为眼前的建设规模太大、合同锁定太深，任何其他融资方式都无法承载。所有人退避三舍的稀释，读对了其实是一个关于机遇体量的信号。我们继续持有 $ORCL 多头，并在下跌中完成建仓。我们认为这接近于一个完美的长期入场点——而且应当受益于日益向 $IGV 软件复合体倾斜的再平衡顺风。

## 甜点

我预计独立日行情会大致按惯例如期而至，就像往常一样——毕竟季末和大部分再平衡压力已经过去。不过七月剩余的时间，读起来像一个真正的谜。我的基础预期是下半年磨砺式的上行趋势——那种我们在 2021 年经历过的、两步向上、一步后退的攀爬。方向向上，但过程不会平顺。

系好安全带。

—— Atros W.M.

title: Neapolitan Shake
excerpt: Like the dessert it’s named for, June arrived with a little bit of everything in the carton — three distinct flavors stacked in the same tub, none of them quite bleeding into the others. So let’s take them one scoop at a time.
content:
# Neapolitan Shake

Like the dessert it’s named for, June arrived with a little bit of everything in the carton — three distinct flavors stacked in the same tub, none of them quite bleeding into the others. So let’s take them one scoop at a time.

![](/blog/june-2026-illustration.png)

## The first scoop: the Fed

The June FOMC was almost aggressively uneventful — no hike, no cut, no news, and, more pointedly, no responsibility. By “no responsibility” I mean that Chair Warsh made it plain that forward guidance is over under his administration, and that communication from the Fed will be deliberately limited going forward. Doesn’t that remind you of Greenspan? Who’s Greenspan? Yes — exactly. That was last century.

I’ll say this without hedging: I disagree with this reform, fully. The old-school, let-the-market-find-its-own-efficiency philosophy of central banking simply does not map onto the era we’re actually in. The market is an order of magnitude more complex than it was during the years when studied opacity passed for wisdom — more reflexive, more leveraged, more wired to every syllable. Cutting the cord and calling it discipline assumes the market is steered and ready for the new jungle. I’m not at all sure it is.

## The second scoop: the data

Both CPI and PCE came in fractionally cooler than expected — not dramatically, but enough to take some heat out of the room. The hike chorus, predictably, has started warming up again. I highly doubt it. If hikes were genuinely on the table, I don’t believe they’d arrive before the midterms. Some songs only get sung after the votes are counted.

## The third scoop: the book

This is where June actually earned its keep.

$NOK gave us the run-up we’d been waiting for, and we took the profit — and then we stepped right back in. We think the name is primed for a revaluation after earnings on July 23rd. The math is uncomplicated: even before a single AI-RAN check clears the account, $NOK ought to be trading at least half of $CIEN’s P/E. It currently isn’t, and that gap is the trade.

$ORCL, by contrast, did not have a good month. In fact it had its worst month since the dot-com bust — a genuinely ugly tape. Why? Because we all hate dilution, and Oracle handed the market a $20 billion equity offering to chew on. But let’s think this through instead of flinching at it. Why do they keep diluting? That’s exactly the catch. You don’t raise that kind of money to tread water; you raise it because the buildout in front of you is too large and too contracted to fund any other way. The dilution everyone is recoiling from is, read correctly, a tell about the size of the opportunity. We remain long $ORCL and we took our position into the weakness. We think this is close to a perfect entry for a long play — and one that should benefit from the rebalancing tailwind that increasingly favors the $IGV software complex.

## And dessert

I expect the Independence Day rally to show up roughly on schedule, the way it usually does, now that quarter-end and the bulk of rebalancing are behind us. The rest of July, though, reads like a genuine mystery. My base case is a bumpy uptrend through the back half of the year — the kind of grinding, two-steps-up-one-step-back climb we lived through in 2021. The direction is up. The ride is not smooth.

Buckle up.

— Atros W.M.

title: 押注
excerpt: 五月算不上出彩，市场也谈不上糟糕。而在这两句话之间的某处缝隙里，我押了一注——如果你读过我以往的这些信，就会明白这是我宁愿白纸黑字写下、也不愿让读者从盘面里自行揣测的那类坦白。
content:
# 押注

五月算不上出彩，市场也谈不上糟糕。而在这两句话之间的某处缝隙里，我押了一注——如果你读过我以往的这些信，就会明白这是我宁愿白纸黑字写下、也不愿让读者从盘面里自行揣测的那类坦白。

![](/blog/may-2026-illustration.png)

## 那一注：$PDD

这一注押在了 $PDD 上。我们预期的那波拉升没有如约而至，复盘下来归结为两点。第一点是结构性的，事后看来再明显不过：$PDD 在美国交易所挂牌，但从任何实质意义上讲它都是一家中国公司，因此它的节奏更贴合恒生指数，而非纳斯达克。整个月里，恒指都在一片低流动性区域中艰难穿行——那种稀薄、令人窒息的盘面，信念在其中得不到奖赏，只会被悄悄无视。第二点是基本面的：监管罚款在净利润率上留下了印记，而市场在留意到别的一切之前，先注意到了这道凹痕。于是那波拉升，就停在了跑道上。

我想说清楚，我并没有要离场的意思。运营一如既往地稳健，增长依然在。对于一家被市场共识屡屡试图盖棺定论的业务而言，Temu 表现得相当不错。我们保持乐观，也继续持有。

## 继续做多 $NOK

账本的另一端，$NOK 继续善待我们，我们维持多头。这一笔我们看的是长周期——我们在为一个建立在 AI-RAN 之上的未来布局，也就是人工智能与无线接入网络的融合。我们宁愿早一点、有耐心，也不愿晚一步、空对。信念，在这里就是全部的意义所在。

与此同时，数据本身几乎没有给自己招来任何关注。一切大致符合预期，宏观叙事维持不变，房间里唯一真正喧闹的，是半导体的那波涨势——视你查看的时刻而定，它已经从令人印象深刻，走向了坦白说有些失控。

## 展望六月

这就把我们带到了六月，一个在纸面上看起来近乎咄咄逼人地平淡的月份。所有目光都聚焦在凯文·沃什（Kevin Warsh）主持的首次 FOMC 会议上，他刚刚走马上任，坐到了那张桌子的主位。真正的问题其实无关点阵图，而在于这位新主席是否懂得风往哪儿吹——以及那个被许诺的"繁荣"究竟能否兑现，还是说它终究只是那种在演讲里听着比在数据里读着更动听的词。我们很快就会知道。

随着篇章翻页，有一个仓位我们正逐渐看好：软件终于得到了热钱的一些青睐，市场似乎也终于重新定位了它评估资本开支的方式——不再把每一块钱的支出都当作一种"招供"，而开始把它读作一次下注。在这一趋势中，我们尤其看好 $ORCL，并计划建仓。

平淡的月份，并不等于安静的月份。我们会保持关注。

—— Atros W.M.

content:
# The Punt

May wasn’t great. The market wasn’t bad. And somewhere in the gap between those two sentences, I punted — which, if you’ve read these letters before, you’ll recognize as the kind of admission I’d rather make in print than have a reader infer from the tape.

![](/blog/may-2026-illustration.png)

## The punt: $PDD

The punt was $PDD. We’d anticipated a spike that didn’t arrive, and the autopsy comes down to two things. The first is structural and, in hindsight, obvious: $PDD trades on a U.S. exchange, but it is a Chinese company in every way that matters, and so it rhymes with the Hang Seng rather than the Nasdaq. The Hang Seng spent the month fighting through a low-liquidity zone — the kind of thin, airless tape where conviction doesn’t get rewarded so much as quietly ignored. The second is fundamental: regulatory fines left a mark on net margin, and the market noticed the dent before it noticed anything else. So the spike sat on the runway.

I want to be clear that I’m not walking away from it. Operations were good, as they reliably are. Growth is still there. Temu is doing perfectly fine for a business that the consensus keeps trying to write the obituary for. We stay optimistic, and we stay in.

## Staying long $NOK

On the other side of the ledger, $NOK continues to treat us well, and we are staying long. This one we love for the long arc — we’re positioning for a future built on AI-RAN, the convergence of artificial intelligence and the radio access network, and we’d rather be early and patient than late and right. Conviction, here, is the whole point.

The data, meanwhile, did very little to draw attention to itself. Everything printed roughly in line, the macro narrative held, and the only genuinely loud thing in the room was the rally in semiconductors — which has gone from impressive to frankly a little unhinged, depending on the hour you check.

## Looking to June

Which brings us to June, a month that looks, on paper, almost aggressively plain. All eyes are on the first FOMC meeting chaired by Kevin Warsh, newly installed at the head of the table. The question isn’t really about the dot plot. It’s whether the new chair knows which way the wind is blowing — and whether the “prosperity” that’s been promised can actually be delivered, or whether it stays the kind of word that sounds better in a speech than it reads in a print. We’ll find out soon enough.

One position we’re warming to as the page turns: software is finally getting some love from the hot money, and it seems the market has at last repositioned how it values CAPEX — no longer treating every dollar of spend as a confession, and starting to read it as a bet. We particularly like $ORCL in this trend, and we plan to take a position.

A plain month is not a quiet one. We’ll be paying attention.

— Atros W.M.

content:
# 恶作剧与玛丽·简

四月，大概率会成为我们2026年表现最佳的月份——我以适度的迷信心态记下这一事实。就叫它"过渡之月"吧。在4月1日第一杯咖啡和30日收盘价之间的某个节点，局面悄然翻转。我们平掉了自一月以来持有的空头仓位，转身站到了多头这边。这个决定并非出于情感。正伽马已经推进到一个不能礼貌地称为"适度"的区域，自营账簿正在以比单纯凭信念坚守更快的速度侵蚀我们在空头端积累的利润。于是，我们动了。

回过头看，当月数据像走地雷阵一样，却没有引爆任何东西。月初的ADP和非农就业数据——干净。CPI——干净。没有任何数据把市场从它自己决定讲述的叙事中拉偏。今日公布的PCE数据是我会标注为"带有隐性风险低频共鸣"的那个，但我不想夸大其词。和近来常见的情况一样，麻烦的根源还是追溯到原油。美联储在所有人预期的位置按兵不动。流动性处于合理水平——没有泛滥，也没有止血带，只是那种平淡无奇、却能让价格发现真正运转起来的水管系统。

![](/blog/april-2026-illustration.png)

## 五月与市场效率

正因如此，我预计五月将是"市场效率之月"。交易商伽马接近中性，当缓冲垫变薄，价格就会开始做它本应做的事情。我预计半导体将出现回调，资金将轮动至其他板块——那种在事后看起来显而易见、在发生当下却令人坐立不安的广度行情。ATROS已相应锚定立场：我们持有中概ADR多头，等待两位王者会面；同时耐心等待重新进入半导体的合适入场点。耐心，在此刻就是仓位本身。

## 结语

最后，写一段与本信其余部分略显错位的文字。我想花一点时间向杰罗姆·鲍威尔致敬。这个人把这个市场——以及我们所有人——从新冠、从不止一次剑拔弩张的局面、从一场接一场本足以压垮一位更不稳健的主席的行政闹剧中拖了出来。在我看来，他是我职业生涯中最被低估、最被忽视的美联储主席。时间，一如既往，会给出答案。

向五月前进。—— ATROS W.M.

content:
# Pranks and Mary Jane

April will, in all likelihood, go down as our best-performing month of 2026 — a fact I note with the appropriate amount of superstition. Call it the month of transition. Somewhere between the first cup of coffee on April 1st and the closing print on the 30th, the book turned. We unwound the short positions we'd been carrying since January and crossed the floor to the bull side. The reasoning wasn't sentimental. Positive gamma had pushed into territory you couldn't politely call moderate, and the prime book was flattening the profits we'd accumulated on the short side faster than conviction alone could justify holding them. So we moved.

The data, in retrospect, walked through a minefield without setting anything off. ADP and nonfarm payrolls at the top of the month — clean. CPI — clean. Nothing that pulled the market off the narrative it had decided to tell itself. Today's PCE print is the one I'd flag as carrying a faint hum of latent risk, though I don't want to overstate it. As is so often the case lately, the trouble traces back to oil. The Fed held rates where everyone expected them to hold rates. Liquidity sits at a reasonable level — no flood, no tourniquet, just the kind of unremarkable plumbing that lets price discovery actually happen.

![](/blog/april-2026-illustration.png)

## May and market efficiency

Which is why I suspect May will be the month of market efficiency. Dealer gamma is sitting close to neutral, and when the cushion thins out, prices start doing the work they're supposed to do. I'd expect a correction in semiconductors and a rotation into other sectors — the kind of breadth event that tends to look obvious in hindsight and feel uncomfortable while it's happening. ATROS is anchored accordingly. We're long Chinese ADRs heading into the meeting between the two kings, and we're waiting, patiently, for the right entry to step back into semis. Patience here is the position.

## A closing note

A closing note, slightly out of register with the rest of this letter. I want to take a moment to express my appreciation for Jerome Powell. The man dragged this market — and by extension, all of us — out of COVID, out of more than one edgy situation, and out of a parade of administrative shit shows that would have broken a less steady chair. He is, in my view, the most underappreciated and underrated Fed chair of my career. Time, as it tends to, will tell.

Onward to May. — ATROS W.M.
